no-binding-proof: Without the embedded two-sided proof the credential is UAI asserting ownership on its own word, which is exactly what section 6.4.1 refuses to do.
one-sided-proof: One signature proves one party's intent. Ownership is a relationship and needs both halves.
no-agent-key-carried: The agent key travels inside the proof so a verifier never has to ask UAI whether the agent exists; without it the proof cannot be checked offline.
ownership-with-expiry: Ownership holds until the agent is unbound, which is an event and not a date. An expiry would mean an agent silently loses the party that answers for it.
half-signed-in-wrong-domain: Each half is a challenge response; a signature made in another domain must not count as one.
